what: iOS 27 UISheetPresentationController drags, flicks and grabber taps driven by synthesized touches on the device (same probe and paths as ../../ios27/sheet-drag)
probe: tool/ios_reference scene w2sheet (Sources/Widgets2.swift) driven by UITests/Widgets2UITests.swift testW2Sheet / testW2SheetFlicks (30 Hz path points); trimmed to the last stroke
rows: start; touch (t, phase 0 down / 1 move / 3 up, x, y); evt (present, detent identifier, dismissed); V = the UIDropShadowView presentation frame (x, y, w, h center/size, bw/bh unscaled bounds)

files.hold.jsonl: a 0.8 s press on the grabber band: the swell, then the lift taps the grabber (medium -> large)
files.drag-*.jsonl, large-drag-*.jsonl, l-drag: slow drags released still (l- = a large-only sheet)
files.flick-up/down.jsonl: short flicks at 600 pt/s from medium
files.fu-N / fd-N / lfd-N.jsonl: flicks of nominal speed N pt/s: up from medium, down from medium (below the smallest detent: return or dismiss), down from large
files.fd-lift-mid.jsonl: a flick down that starts in the sheet body
files.l-flick-down.jsonl: a flick down on a large-only sheet (dismisses)

boundary: fd-1000 (887 pt/s, stays) and lfd-800 (714 pt/s, settles at large) sit on the decision boundary; the replay test leaves them out
units: points (pt), window coordinates, seconds on the device media clock
